newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian bonds stay close to day's highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian bonds stay close to day's highs.

text.p: *Australian bonds stayed close to the day's highs after pressing against resistance on futures and on the yield differential against the U.S..
*There was no major local data released on Thursday.
Australian bonds maintained its bullish tone of the last few days, pressing against resistance on futures, and also on the yield differential against the U.S..

However, traders felt the market may have got a little ahead of itself with the U.S. market still proving the overriding factor ahead of next week's FOMC meeting, where the possibilty of a policy tightening by the Fed continues to haunt.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see us retrace a little from here ahead of another stack of figures out of the U.S. tonight," one trader added.
There was no major local data released today.

Scant talk of another dual currency samurai bond issue helped to fuel the market's bullish tone, which remains geared up for a further interest rate cut before the end of the year, and saw bond futures closing in on this week's highs.
The market was also tackling resistance on the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread at around 110 basis points, to stand some 15 basis points down from Monday.
Meanwhile, Queensland Treasury Corp held a A$100 million domestic bond tender of its September 2007 stock, which fetched a yield of 8.076 percent with succesful bids in a tight 1.5 basis point range.

Local bonds also outperformed Canadian debt where supply pressures weighed on the market after its 10-year bond auction. The New Zealand market continued to benefit from a strong N.Z. dollar, reclaiming some of its recent lost ground against other dollar bonds.
